question: People born without the Nav1.7 sodium channel feel no pain. What gave one such woman pain in 2015?
answer: Naloxone, the drug that reverses opioid overdoses. Losing Nav1.7 also makes sensory nerves produce more of the body's own opioids, enkephalins. When London researchers blocked them with naloxone, she felt pain for the first time. It helps explain why pure Nav1.7 blockers, long a hoped-for painkiller, disappointed in trials.
move: A missing part can work through what the body builds to cope.
ask: What missing piece in my life works through something I built to cope?
